# Web (22 endpoints)

## Endpoints

| Resource | Params | Credits | Description |
|----------|--------|---------|-------------|
| /scrape | `url` | **1-5** | Scrape a web page |
| /search | `query` | **2-120** | Search the web |
| /map | `url` | 1 | Map URLs on a site |
| /extract | `url`, `schema` / `prompt` | **5** | Extract structured data from a web page |
| **POST** /crawl | `url` | **1-10000** | Start an async web crawl |
| **POST** /batch-scrape | `urls` | **no ceiling** | Start an async batch scrape |
| /jobs | `limit`?, `cursor`? | 0 | List async web jobs |
| /jobs/{job_id} | `job_id` | 0 | Get an async web job |
| **DELETE** /jobs/{job_id} | `job_id` | 0 | Cancel an async web job |
| **POST** /agent | `url`, `prompt` | 25 | Start an async web agent job |
| **POST** /monitors | `url` | **no ceiling** | Create a web monitor |
| /monitors | `cursor`?, `limit`? | 0 | List web monitors |
| /monitors/{monitor_id} | `monitor_id` | 0 | Get a web monitor |
| **PATCH** /monitors/{monitor_id} | `monitor_id` | 0 | Update a web monitor |
| **DELETE** /monitors/{monitor_id} | `monitor_id` | 0 | Delete a web monitor |
| /monitors/{monitor_id}/checks | `monitor_id` | 0 | List web monitor checks |
| **POST** /sessions | `url` | **no ceiling** | Create an interactive web session |
| /sessions | `limit`? | 0 | List interactive web sessions |
| /sessions/{session_id} | `session_id` | 0 | Get an interactive web session |
| **DELETE** /sessions/{session_id} | `session_id` | 0 | Close an interactive web session |

| **POST** /parse | `file` | 1 | Parse an uploaded document |

### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /scrape — 1-5cr

Fetches a public web page and returns clean content, metadata, and optional media in the unified WebPage schema.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 1-5 credits a call — budget the 5 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 1-5 (metered): 1 credit for a standard scrape. It rises to a flat 5 when the fetch needs more than a plain request: `proxy=auto`, `proxy=enhanced`, or `pdf_parse=true`. Nothing else moves the price, so screenshots, tag filters, `wait_for` and a mobile viewport are all included in the 1 credit

**Parameters**

- `url`: Public URL to fetch.
- `formats` *(optional)*: Comma-separated output formats such as markdown,screenshot.
- `only_main_content` *(optional)*: Strip nav, headers, footers and sidebars and keep the article body. Default true; send false when you need the whole page, including the chrome. A markdown-only scrape of a site the primary scraper cannot fetch is served by a second extractor, which returns the whole page.
- `wait_for` *(optional)*: Milliseconds to wait after load before capturing, for pages that render their content in JavaScript. Leave unset unless the page comes back empty or half-built.
- `mobile` *(optional)*: Render in a mobile viewport with a mobile user agent. Use it when the site serves a different layout to phones.
- `timeout` *(optional)*: Hard cap on the page load in milliseconds, 1 to 30000. A page that exceeds it fails and is refunded rather than returning a partial capture.
- `max_age` *(optional)*: Accept an upstream-cached copy up to this many milliseconds old, which is faster and still one credit. Default 172800000 (48 hours); send 0 to force a live fetch.
- `location_country` *(optional)*: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code to fetch from, e.g. 'us' or 'de'. Use it for geo-varying pages such as pricing or availability.
- `screenshot_full_page` *(optional)*: When a screenshot format is requested, capture the entire scrollable page instead of the visible viewport.
- `include_tags` *(optional)*: CSV of CSS selectors or HTML tags to keep, e.g. 'article,main'. Everything outside them is dropped. Use it to pin extraction to a known container.
- `exclude_tags` *(optional)*: CSV of CSS selectors or HTML tags to drop, e.g. 'nav,footer,.cookie-banner'. Applied after include_tags.
- `proxy` *(optional)*: Proxy tier: basic, auto, or enhanced.
- `pdf_parse` *(optional)*: Parse the target as a PDF and return its extracted text. Send it when the URL points at a PDF rather than an HTML page.
- `block_ads` *(optional)*: Block ad and tracker requests, which is faster and quieter. Default true.
- `remove_base64_images` *(optional)*: Drop inline base64-encoded images from the returned content instead of carrying them in the payload. Default true.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/scrape?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /search — 2-120cr

Searches web, news, and image sources and returns a single normalized list of web page results.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 2-120 credits a call — budget the 120 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 2-120 (metered): 2 credits per 10 results, so `limit` up to 10 costs 2, 11-20 costs 4, and the 100 maximum costs 20. `include_content=true` adds 1 credit per result, because it scrapes each result page as well as reading the SERP row - that is what takes a 100-result content search to the 120-credit ceiling. The hold settles down to the work actually done

**Parameters**

- `query`: Search query.
- `sources` *(optional)*: Comma-separated sources: web,news,images.
- `categories` *(optional)*: CSV of source categories to restrict the search to, e.g. 'github,research'. Omit for an unrestricted web search.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Results per source, from 1 to 100.
- `country` *(optional)*: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code the search is run from, e.g. 'US' (default) or 'GB'. Changes which results rank.
- `location` *(optional)*: Free-text locality to bias results towards, e.g. 'London, United Kingdom'. Finer-grained than country.
- `time_range` *(optional)*: Recency window as a Google `tbs` value: 'qdr:d' past day, 'qdr:w' past week, 'qdr:m' past month, 'qdr:y' past year.
- `sort_by_date` *(optional)*: Sort newest-first instead of by relevance. Combines with time_range rather than replacing it.
- `include_domains` *(optional)*: CSV of domains to restrict results to, e.g. 'nytimes.com,ft.com'. Cannot be combined with exclude_domains - sending both is a 400 before billing.
- `exclude_domains` *(optional)*: CSV of domains to drop from the results. Cannot be combined with include_domains.
- `include_content` *(optional)*: Also scrape each result and return its page content as markdown, not just the SERP row. This is what makes the call expensive: it scrapes one page per result, which is why the range runs to 120 credits.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/search?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /map — 1cr

Discovers URLs for a public site and returns them as a normalized WebPageList.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Site URL to map.
- `search` *(optional)*: Optional path or keyword filter.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Maximum URLs to return, up to 5000.
- `sitemap` *(optional)*: How to use the site's sitemap.xml: 'include' (default) to merge it with crawled links, 'only' to trust it alone, 'skip' to ignore it.
- `include_subdomains` *(optional)*: Follow links onto subdomains of the root URL. Default true.
- `ignore_query_parameters` *(optional)*: Treat URLs differing only by query string as one URL, which keeps paginated and tracking-tagged duplicates out of the result. Default true.
- `fresh` *(optional)*: Bypass the upstream cache and re-discover the site now. Slower; use it when the map is known to be stale.
- `goal` *(optional)*: Optional. What you are looking for on the site, in your own words. The map still returns every URL, ranked, with skipped_urls listing the ones that look unlikely to hold it (each with p). Without this param the map is unchanged.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/map?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /extract — 5cr

Fetches one web page and returns structured extraction output under the WebPage extraction field.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 5 credits a call — budget the 5 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 5 (metered): A flat 5 credits. It runs through the metered pricer for consistency with the rest of the web surface, but nothing in your query changes the charge

**Parameters**

- `url`: Public URL to extract from.
- `only_main_content` *(optional)*: Strip nav, headers, footers and sidebars and keep the article body. Default true; send false when you need the whole page, including the chrome.
- `timeout` *(optional)*: Hard cap on each page load in milliseconds, 1 to 30000. A page that exceeds it fails and is refunded rather than returning a partial capture.
- `max_age` *(optional)*: Accept an upstream-cached copy up to this many milliseconds old, which is faster and costs the same. Default 172800000 (48 hours); send 0 to force a live fetch.
- `proxy` *(optional)*: Proxy tier: basic, auto, or enhanced. Raise it only when a site blocks the default tier - enhanced is slower.
- `schema` / `prompt` — at least one required.
  - `schema`: JSON object schema describing the data to return. (one of: schema, prompt; at least one required)
  - `prompt`: Plain-language extraction instruction. (one of: schema, prompt; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/extract?url=<url>&schema=<schema>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

> ⚠️ **Metered: 1-10000 credits a call — budget the 10000 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 1-10000 (metered): 1 credit per page crawled. Submitting holds `limit` credits up front (default limit 10, max 10,000) and the unused portion is refunded when the job settles

**Parameters**

- `url` *(body)*: 
- `limit` *(body, optional)*: 
- `max_depth` *(body, optional)*: 
- `allow_backward_links` *(body, optional)*: 
- `allow_external_links` *(body, optional)*: 
- `include_paths` *(body, optional)*: 
- `exclude_paths` *(body, optional)*:

### /jobs/{job_id} — 0cr

Returns the current status, billing settlement, progress, and any available result metadata for one async web job: crawl, batch scrape, or agent. Append /errors to the same path to list per-page failures and robots-blocked URLs (crawl and batch scrape jobs).

**Parameters**

- `job_id`: Job id (job_...) returned by POST /v1/web/crawl, POST /v1/web/batch-scrape, or POST /v1/web/agent as data.job_id.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/jobs/<job_id>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

Cancels one async web job of any kind (crawl, batch scrape, or agent), closes the upstream work when possible, and refunds any unsettled held credits.

**Parameters**

- `job_id`: Job id (job_...) returned by POST /v1/web/crawl, POST /v1/web/batch-scrape, or POST /v1/web/agent as data.job_id.


### **POST** /monitors — no ceiling

Creates an upstream-backed monitor. Creation is free; every scheduled check bills its upstream cost plus 1 credit for orchestration, and keeps billing on the cadence you set until the monitor is paused or deleted. The response returns credits_booked, the upstream cost of a single check, so budget (credits_booked + 1) x checks per month before leaving one running.

> ⚠️ **No ceiling can be computed for this call — the credit guard asks before every one.** Vendor label: 0 credits to create. Each scheduled check then bills its upstream cost plus 1 credit for orchestration, repeating on `cadence_minutes` until you pause or delete the monitor (a 5-minute cadence is 288 checks a day)

**Parameters**

- `url` *(body)*: 
- `name` *(body, optional)*: 
- `mode` *(body, optional)*: 
- `cadence_minutes` *(body, optional)*: 
- `schedule_text` *(body, optional)*: 
- `schedule_cron` *(body, optional)*: 
- `timezone` *(body, optional)*: 
- `webhook_url` *(body, optional)*: 
- `query` *(body, optional)*: 
- `goal` *(body, optional)*: 
- `retention_days` *(body, optional)*: 
- `judge_enabled` *(body, optional)*: 

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/monitors" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "<url>"}'
```

## Choosing a web endpoint

This is the general-purpose crawler — reach for it when the answer lives on a site that has
no platform endpoint of its own (a personal domain, a linktree that `prism/lookup` can't
resolve, a docs page, a pricing page).

| Your goal | Use this | Credits |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| One page's content, right now | `/scrape` | 1 |
| A keyword search of the open web | `/search` | 2 |
| What URLs exist on this site? | `/map` | 1 |
| Pull named fields out of a page (price, headline, offer) | `/extract` | 5 |
| Many pages / a whole site | `POST /crawl` or `POST /batch-scrape` → poll `/jobs/{job_id}` | 1 |
| Watch a page for changes over time | `POST /monitors` | 0 |
| Click, type, and navigate a page | `POST /sessions` then `POST /sessions/{id}/execute` | 5 to open, 0 per action |
| Turn an uploaded PDF/doc into text | `POST /parse` | 1 |
| Nothing above worked and the task needs judgement | `POST /agent` | **25** |

### Cost shape — most of this platform is free

The async machinery is 0cr: listing jobs, polling `/jobs/{job_id}`, cancelling, and every
monitor and session operation except opening the session. You pay to *start* work
(`crawl`/`batch-scrape` 1cr, `sessions` 5cr, `agent` 25cr), not to supervise it. Poll job
status as often as you like.

`/scrape` at 1cr is the workhorse. Before escalating, ask whether one page would answer the
question — `/extract` (5cr) is `/scrape` plus structured field-pulling, so if you are going to
read the page yourself anyway, scrape it.

### POST /agent is the most expensive call in the entire API

25 credits, one call. It is an agentic browse-and-extract job for cases where you cannot say
in advance which pages to visit. Confirm the spend with the user every time — no exceptions,
and never in a loop. If you can name the URLs, `batch-scrape` (1cr) does the job for a
twenty-fifth of the price.

### Async jobs

`POST /crawl`, `POST /batch-scrape` and `POST /agent` return a `job_id` (`job_...`) rather
than results. Poll `GET /jobs/{job_id}` (0cr) until it settles, or register a `webhook_url` in
the request body and skip polling. Append `/errors` to the job path to see per-page failures
and robots-blocked URLs. Cancel with `DELETE /jobs/{job_id}` (0cr).

### Sessions are stateful and cost per session, not per action

`POST /sessions` (5cr) opens an interactive browser session; each `POST
/sessions/{id}/execute` is free. That inverts the usual math: a multi-step interaction
(accept a dialog, paginate, click through a gate) costs a flat 5cr no matter how many steps.
Close it with `DELETE /sessions/{session_id}` when done. Note the cost asymmetry — `GET
/sessions` is free, `POST /sessions` is 5cr.
